subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt provider-level fail-closed cooldown state for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, including the durable `inline-api-key:<provider>` usage identity?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the persisted identity, recovery behavior, and fail-closed upgrade effect are auth-provider compatibility choices that automation should not settle alone.

options.title: Accept provider-level inline cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline provider keys get billing/auth cooldown protection equivalent to profile-backed credentials.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Document migration to auth profiles as the supported workaround and close the linked implementation path as not planned.

options.title: Request a narrower auth design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers specify the exact cooldown identity, persistence, and recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level inline cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline provider keys get billing/auth cooldown protection equivalent to profile-backed credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed routing signal for compatibility-sensitive auth/provider behavior from current history and timeline mentions.
